74130-prize-of-the-air.title: Prize Of The Air
74130-prize-of-the-air.creator: Ben Conlon
74130-prize-of-the-air.description: A book by Ben Conlon. But Bill Barlow didn’t seem to mind. A man who can laugh in the face of death is not to be disturbed by such a trifle as the revocation of a license. It was Saxton, his passenger, who seemed the more concerned. He approached Bill later that afternoon.

arxiv-1707-07489.title: Oscillations for Equivalence Preservation and Information Retrieval from Young Black Holes
arxiv-1707-07489.creator: Alexander Y. Yosifov, Lachezar G. Filipov
arxiv-1707-07489.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Alexander Y. Yosifov, Lachezar G. Filipov. We follow the prevailing view that black holes do not destroy but rather process and release information in the form of Hawking radiation. By making certain conservative assumptions regarding the interior dynamics of the quantum system we suggest an outside observer could, in principle, recover the initial quantum state | ψ ⟩ \left|\psi\right\rangle before the black hole has evaporated half of its entropy.

arxiv-2106-10186.title: An analytical model for tidal evolution in co-orbital systems
arxiv-2106-10186.creator: Jérémy Couturier, Philippe Robutel, Alexandre C. M. Correia
arxiv-2106-10186.description: Abstract Close-in co-orbital planets (in a 1:1 mean motion resonance) can experience strong tidal interactions with the central star. Here, we develop an analytical model adapted to the study of the tidal evolution of those systems. We use a Hamiltonian version of the constant time-lag tidal model, which extends the Hamiltonian formalism developed for the point-mass case.

arxiv-2112-14589.title: Demonstration of multi-qubit entanglement and algorithms on a programmable neutral atom quantum computer
arxiv-2112-14589.creator: T. M. Graham, Y. Song, J. Scott, C. Poole, L. Phuttitarn, K. Jooya, P. Eichler, X. Jiang, A. Marra, B. Grinkemeyer, M. Kwon, M. Ebert, J. Cherek, M. T. Lichtman, M. Gillette, J. Gilbert, D. Bowman, T. Ballance, C. Campbell, E. D. Dahl, O. Crawford, N. S. Blunt, B. Rogers, T. Noel, M. Saffman
arxiv-2112-14589.description: Abstract Gate model quantum computers promise to solve currently intractable computational problems if they can be operated at scale with long coherence times and high fidelity logic. Neutral atom hyperfine qubits provide inherent scalability due to their identical characteristics, long coherence times, and ability to be trapped in dense multi-dimensional arrays Saffman et al. 2010 .

arxiv-2205-07814.title: Punctured-Chern topological invariants for semi-metallic bandstructures
arxiv-2205-07814.creator: Ankur Das, Eyal Cornfeld, Sumiran Pujari
arxiv-2205-07814.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ankur Das, Eyal Cornfeld, Sumiran Pujari. Topological insulator-based methods underpin the topological classification of gapped bands, including those surrounding semi-metallic nodal defects. However, multiple bands with gap-closing points can also possess non-trivial topology. We construct a general wavefunction-based “punctured-Chern” invariant to capture such topology.

arxiv-2208-08278.title: MSW effect with quark matter: Neutron Star as a case study
arxiv-2208-08278.creator: Hiranmaya Mishra, Prasanta K. Panigrahi, Sudhanwa Patra, Utpal Sarkar
arxiv-2208-08278.description: Abstract With the recent findings from various astrophysical results hinting towards possible existence of strange quark matters with the baryonic resonances such as Λ 0 , Σ 0 , Ξ , Ω \Lambda^{0},\Sigma^{0},\Xi,\Omega in the core of neutron stars, we investigate the MSW effect, in general, in quark matter.

arxiv-2208-11926.title: Dynamic collaborative filtering Thompson Sampling for cross-domain advertisements recommendation Conference: ; August 15, 2022; Washington, D.C.
arxiv-2208-11926.creator: Shion Ishikawa, Young-joo Chung, Yu Hirate
arxiv-2208-11926.description: Abstract . Recently online advertisers utilize Recommender systems (RSs) for display advertising to improve users’ engagement. Contextual bandit model is a widely used RS to exploit and explore users’ engagement and maximize the long-term rewards such as clicks or conversions.

arxiv-2307-07109.title: Laboratory Study of Collisionless Magnetic Reconnection
arxiv-2307-07109.creator: H. Ji, J. Yoo, W. Fox, M. Yamada, M. Argall, J. Egedal, Y.-H. Liu, R. Wilder, S. Eriksson, W. Daughton, K. Bergstedt, S. Bose, J. Burch, R. Torbert, J. Ng, L.-J. Chen
arxiv-2307-07109.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by H. Ji, J. Yoo, W. Fox, M. Yamada, M. Argall, J. Egedal, Y.-H. Liu, R. Wilder, S. Eriksson, W. Daughton, K. Bergstedt, S. Bose, J. Burch, R. Torbert, J. Ng, L.-J. Chen. A concise review is given on the past two decades’ results from laboratory experiments on collisionless magnetic reconnection in direct relation with space measurements, especially by Magnetospheric Multiscale (MMS) mission.

arxiv-2309-06009.title: Content Reduction, Surprisal and Information Density Estimation for Long Documents
arxiv-2309-06009.creator: Shaoxiong Ji, Wei Sun, Pekka Marttinen
arxiv-2309-06009.description: Abstract Many computational linguistic methods have been proposed to study the information content of languages. We consider two interesting research questions: 1) how is information distributed over long documents, and 2) how does content reduction, such as token selection and text summarization, affect the information density in long documents.

arxiv-2407-09496.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network based inverse framework for time-fractional differential equations for rheology
arxiv-2407-09496.creator: Sukirt Thakur, Harsa Mitra, Arezoo M. Ardekani
arxiv-2407-09496.description: Abstract Time-fractional differential equations offer a robust framework for capturing intricate phenomena characterized by memory effects, particularly in fields like biotransport and rheology. However, solving inverse problems involving fractional derivatives presents notable challenges, including issues related to stability and uniqueness.

arxiv-2408-08971.title: A Multi-Task and Multi-Label Classification Model for Implicit Discourse Relation Recognition
arxiv-2408-08971.creator: Nelson Filipe Costa, Leila Kosseim
arxiv-2408-08971.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nelson Filipe Costa, Leila Kosseim. We propose a novel multi-label classification approach to implicit discourse relation recognition (IDRR). Our approach features a multi-task model that jointly learns multi-label representations of implicit discourse relations across all three sense levels in the PDTB 3.0 framework. The model can also be adapted to the traditional single-label IDRR setting by selecting the sense with the highest probability in the multi-label representation. We conduct extensive experiments to identify optimal model configurations and loss functions in both settings.

arxiv-2411-14734.title: Ab initio study of orbital-selective superconductivity in γ \gamma -BiPd
arxiv-2411-14734.creator: Sonu Prasad Keshri, Guang-Yu Guo
arxiv-2411-14734.description: Abstract We investigate the superconducting (SC) properties of experimentally realised γ \gamma -BiPd by solving the anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg equations in conjunction with ab initio relativistic calculations of the electron and phonon band structures as well as electron-phonon coupling (EPC) matrix elements.

arxiv-2506-02134.title: ReconXF: Graph Reconstruction Attack via Public Feature Explanations on Privatized Node Features and Labels
arxiv-2506-02134.creator: Rishi Raj Sahoo, Rucha Bhalchandra Joshi, Subhankar Mishra
arxiv-2506-02134.description: Abstract . Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) achieve high performance across many applications but function as black-box models, limiting their use in critical domains like healthcare and criminal justice. Explainability methods address this by providing feature-level explanations that identify important node attributes for predictions. These explanations create privacy risks.

arxiv-2511-00341.title: Reversal Invariance A symmetry argument against the arrow of chain-of-thought
arxiv-2511-00341.creator: Mihir Sahasrabudhe
arxiv-2511-00341.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mihir Sahasrabudhe. We formalize a structural property of the causal (autoregressive) language modeling (CLM) objective: reversal invariance. Formally, the next-token prediction loss assigns identical likelihood to a corpus and its reversal, implying that standard CLM pretraining is direction-blind. This symmetry explains why models trained on reversed text can achieve comparable performance to those trained on forward text, despite the inherently time-asymmetric nature of human language and reasoning. We argue that this invariance represents a limitation of current pretraining objectives rather than a benign artifact.

arxiv-2601-09975.title: Einstein & Yang–Mills implies Conformal Yang–Mills X
arxiv-2601-09975.creator: Samuel Blitz ♢ , A. Rod Gover ♡ , Jarosław Kopiński ♣ , & Andrew Waldron ♠
arxiv-2601-09975.description: Abstract . There exist conformally invariant, higher-derivative, variational analogs of the Yang–Mills condition for connections on vector bundles over a conformal manifold of even dimension greater than or equal to six. We give a compact formula for these analogs and prove that they are a strict weakening of the Yang–Mills condition with respect to an Einstein metric.

The Tafel slopes used to evaluate the...

pmc-10570852.title: The deubiquitinase ZRANB1 is an E3 ubiquitin ligase for SLC7A11 and regulates ferroptotic resistance
pmc-10570852.creator: Shan Huang, Qimin Zhang, Manyu Zhao, Xing Wang, Yilei Zhang, Boyi Gan, Peijing Zhang
pmc-10570852.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). report that ZRANB1, an OTU family DUB, ubiquitinates and represses SLC7A11 expression as an E3 ubiquitin ligase and that ZRANB1 inhibits glutathione (GSH) synthesis through SLC7A11 degradation, leading to elevated lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis. Introduction

Ferroptosis is usually a regulated form of cell death induced by inactivating lipid repair enzymes such as glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and accumulating lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS) such as lipid hydroperoxides (Yang and Stockwell, 2016). Currently, multiple markers have been developed to detect ferroptotic cells.

pmc-10673401.title: Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 in Chronic Hepatitis C: A Potential Non-Invasive Biomarker of Liver Status upon Viral Eradication
pmc-10673401.creator: Filippo Biagi, Francesco Carlomagno, Martina Carbone, Roberta Veralli, Umberto Vespasiani-Gentilucci, Elisabetta Riva, Silvia Manfrini, Dario Tuccinardi, Adriano De Santis, Lucio Gnessi, Mikiko Watanabe, Amedeo Lonardo
pmc-10673401.description: Fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF-21), previously recognized as a marker of liver damage and a potential drug target in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), has unclear implications in hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections. This study aimed to investigate the relationship between FGF-21 levels and liver health in patients with HCV undergoing direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment.

pmc-11774846.title: Analysis of engineered T7 bacteriophages containing genetic sequences encoding antimicrobial peptides
pmc-11774846.creator: Tobias Ludwig, Daniela Volke, Andor Krizsan
pmc-11774846.description: Because of the global spread of multi- and pan-resistant bacteria, there is a need to identify, research, and develop new strategies to combat these pathogens. In a previous proof-of-concept study, we presented an innovative strategy by genetically modifying lytic T7 bacteriophages.

pmc-12464786.title: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing Therapy in Persons With Personality Disorders
pmc-12464786.creator: Simon Hofman, Laurian Hafkemeijer, Ad de Jongh, Cristina W. Slotema
pmc-12464786.description: Key PointsQuestionDoes eye movement desensitization and reprocessing (EMDR) therapy reduce personality disorder (PD) symptoms, regardless of posttraumatic stress disorder status?FindingsIn this randomized clinical trial including 159 patients with PD, results of EMDR therapy were superior to those of a waiting-list control group in reducing PD symptoms post treatment and at follow-up.

pmc-13231152.title: Patients referred to but not taken on to an outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) service: the impact of infection specialist advice on the assessment and clinical outcomes
pmc-13231152.creator: Mary Rimbi, Simon Pybus, Sophie Dodds, Beth White, Neil Ritchie, R Andrew Seaton
pmc-13231152.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThis study explored antimicrobial stewardship opportunities, clinical impact and patient outcomes in those referred to an outpatient parenteral antimicrobial therapy (OPAT) service, screened by an infection specialist but not taken on in a large tertiary centre.MethodsAll OPAT referrals that were screened but not taken on by the NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde OPAT service over a 3 year period (2022–2024) were reviewed.

pmc-13236746.title: Experiment-based calibration: Inference and decision-making
pmc-13236746.creator: Federico Mancinelli, Dominik R. Bach
pmc-13236746.description: Experiment-based calibration is an emerging approach for measurement validation in the behavioural sciences. It allows comparing multiple measurement methods by how well they reproduce a known experimental manipulation, providing insight into their measurement accuracy. Calibration entails questions unparalleled in classical validation approaches.

pmc-13241498.title: Spontaneous perceptual reversals are accompanied by systematic changes in pupil size but not respiration phase
pmc-13241498.creator: Lisa Stetza, Christoph Kayser
pmc-13241498.description: Humans tend to align their respiration with important events, in line with the notion that respiration serves as a tool to allocate (neuro-)physiological resources. This respiration alignment is consistently reported in laboratory studies relying on sequences of temporally structured, stimulus-driven experimental trials.

pmc-13411534.title: Cannabidiol enhances tamoxifen efficacy via CREB-mediated suppression of ERα signaling in ER-positive breast cancer cells
pmc-13411534.creator: Bu Gyeom Kim, Okhyeon Kim, Do-Yeon Lee, Bo Ram Kim, Dae Yeong Kim, Yoon Namgung, Jun Woo Bong, Sanghee Kang, Sun Il Lee, Sang Cheul Oh
pmc-13411534.description: BackgroundEstrogen receptor alpha (ERα) plays a crucial role in the proliferation and survival of ER-positive breast cancer cells, and tamoxifen (TAM) remains the mainstay of endocrine therapy. However, acquired resistance to TAM remains a major clinical challenge. Despite advances in molecular profiling and targeted therapies, the mechanisms underlying TAM resistance remain incompletely understood.

pmc-13533649.title: Efficacy of a Disposable Skin‐Stretch Closure Device Combined With Vacuum Sealing Drainage in the Treatment of Refractory Skin and Soft Tissue Defects: A Single‐Arm Prospective Study
pmc-13533649.creator: Hao Guo, Zhengguo Zhu, Jinchang Wang, Zhonghe Wang, Yilin Wang, Jun Zhang, Wei Zhang, Guangping Liu, Zhiguang Chen, Shuangcheng Li, Xingxing Hu, Meijing Dou, Junjun Tang, Peifu Tang, Hua Chen
pmc-13533649.description: ObjectivesThe treatment of refractory skin and soft tissue defects (RSSTDs) has long posed a global challenge for surgeons. Traditional closure methods, such as skin grafting and flap repair, are often associated with significant trauma and a steep learning curve. Skin stretching, which enables the generation of “extra skin,” has emerged as a promising alternative.

pmc-13647759.title: Major protease inhibitor drug resistance mutations among patients with virological failure on second-line antiretroviral therapy in Zimbabwe: a retrospective cross-sectional study
pmc-13647759.creator: Justin Mayini, Tendai Washaya, Justen Manasa, Edward Zumbika, Shungu Munyati, Ryman Shoko, Christine Dahlke, Vinie Kouamou
pmc-13647759.description: BackgroundVirological failure (VF) on protease inhibitor (PI)-based second-line antiretroviral therapy (ART) remains an important driver of HIV drug resistance (HIVDR) in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite widespread adoption of dolutegravir (DTG)-based first-line ART, many people living with HIV (PLWH) remain on PI-based second-line regimens. Data on major PI drug resistance mutations (DRMs) in Zimbabwe remain limited.
